The **2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Kentucky** were held on November 8, 2022, to elect the six [U.S. representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") from the [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky"), one from each of the state's six [congressional districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky's_congressional_districts "Kentucky's congressional districts"). The elections coincided with [other elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "2022 United States House of Representatives elections") to the House of Representatives, [elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_Senate_elections "2022 United States Senate elections") to the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") and various [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_elections#State_elections "2022 United States elections") and [local elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_elections#Local_elections "2022 United States elections").

The 1st district takes in Western Kentucky, including [Paducah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paducah,_Kentucky "Paducah, Kentucky"), [Hopkinsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hopkinsville,_Kentucky "Hopkinsville, Kentucky"), [Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray,_Kentucky "Murray, Kentucky"), and [Henderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henderson,_Kentucky "Henderson, Kentucky"). The incumbent was Republican [James Comer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer "James Comer"), who had represented the 1st district since 2016. Comer was most recently re-elected in 2022, winning 74.9% of the vote.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_Kentucky#cite_note-1)

The **2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Kentucky** were held on November 8, 2022, to elect the six [U.S. representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") from the [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky"), one from each of the state's six [congressional districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky's_congressional_districts "Kentucky's congressional districts"). The elections coincided with [other elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "2022 United States House of Representatives elections") to the House of Representatives, [elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_Senate_elections "2022 United States Senate elections") to the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") and various [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_elections#State_elections "2022 United States elections") and [local elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_elections#Local_elections "2022 United States elections").

The 1st district takes in Western Kentucky, including [Paducah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paducah,_Kentucky "Paducah, Kentucky"), [Hopkinsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hopkinsville,_Kentucky "Hopkinsville, Kentucky"), [Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray,_Kentucky "Murray, Kentucky"), and [Henderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henderson,_Kentucky "Henderson, Kentucky"). The incumbent was Republican [James Comer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer "James Comer"), who had represented the 1st district since 2016. Comer was most recently re-elected in 2022, winning 74.9% of the vote.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_Kentucky#cite_note-1)

The **2022 United States House of Representatives elections in West Virginia** were held on November 8, 2022, to elect the two [U.S. representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") from the [State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia "West Virginia"), one from each of the state's two [congressional districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia's_congressional_districts "West Virginia's congressional districts"). The elections coincided with [other elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "2022 United States House of Representatives elections") to the House of Representatives, [elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_Senate_elections "2022 United States Senate elections") to the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"), and various [state and local elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_elections "2022 United States elections").

District boundaries were redrawn to ensure that the districts are [apportioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_congressional_apportionment "United States congressional apportionment") based on data from the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), which eliminated a congressional district in West Virginia's delegation.

See also: [West Virginia's 2nd congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia's_2nd_congressional_district "West Virginia's 2nd congressional district")

The 2nd district encompasses the industrial areas of the [northern Panhandle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Panhandle_of_West_Virginia "Northern Panhandle of West Virginia") including [Wheeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheeling,_West_Virginia "Wheeling, West Virginia"), [Fairmont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairmont,_West_Virginia "Fairmont, West Virginia"), [Clarksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarksburg,_West_Virginia "Clarksburg, West Virginia"), [Morgantown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgantown,_West_Virginia "Morgantown, West Virginia") and [Parkersburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkersburg,_West_Virginia "Parkersburg, West Virginia"), as well as the [eastern Panhandle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Panhandle_of_West_Virginia "Eastern Panhandle of West Virginia"). The incumbents from the district's two predecessor districts are Republican [David McKinley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_McKinley "David McKinley") (who was re-elected in the [1st district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia's_1st_congressional_district "West Virginia's 1st congressional district") with 69.0% of the vote in 2020) and Republican [Alex Mooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mooney "Alex Mooney") (who was re-elected in the [2nd district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia's_2nd_congressional_district "West Virginia's 2nd congressional district") with 63.1% of the vote in 2020).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_West_Virginia#cite_note-clerk2020-1)

The **2022 United States House of Representatives elections in West Virginia** were held on November 8, 2022, to elect the two [U.S. representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") from the [State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia "West Virginia"), one from each of the state's two [congressional districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia's_congressional_districts "West Virginia's congressional districts"). The elections coincided with [other elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "2022 United States House of Representatives elections") to the House of Representatives, [elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_Senate_elections "2022 United States Senate elections") to the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"), and various [state and local elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_elections "2022 United States elections").

District boundaries were redrawn to ensure that the districts are [apportioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_congressional_apportionment "United States congressional apportionment") based on data from the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), which eliminated a congressional district in West Virginia's delegation.

The incumbent was Republican [Carol Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carol_Miller_(politician) "Carol Miller (politician)"), who was re-elected in the [3rd district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia's_3rd_congressional_district "West Virginia's 3rd congressional district") with 71.3% of the vote in 2020.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_West_Virginia#cite_note-clerk2020-1)

**James Richardson Comer Jr.**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-VoteSmart-3) ([/ˈ k oʊ m ər/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_KOH-mər_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born August 19, 1972) is an American politician serving as the [U.S. Representative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Representative "U.S. Representative") for [Kentucky's 1st congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky's_1st_congressional_district "Kentucky's 1st congressional district"). A member of the [Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"), he has served in Congress since 2016, during the [114th United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/114th_United_States_Congress "114th United States Congress"). He previously served in the [Kentucky House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_House_of_Representatives "Kentucky House of Representatives") and also served as the [agriculture commissioner of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture_Commissioner_of_Kentucky "Agriculture Commissioner of Kentucky").

As the chair of the [Oversight Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_Oversight_and_Government_Reform "United States House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform") from 2023, Comer has declined or stopped investigations into former president [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump"), while starting an investigation on President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") and his family. As of August 2024, Comer's investigation has yet to unearth evidence that Biden was directly involved in or profited from his family's business activities.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Praveena-4) After Biden ended his 2024 presidential re-election campaign, Comer began an investigation into the new Democratic presidential nominee, Vice President [Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris"), and also began an investigation into the new Democratic vice-presidential nominee, Governor [Tim Walz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Walz "Tim Walz").

Comer served as Kentucky's agriculture commissioner from 2012 to 2016 and in the [Kentucky House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_House_of_Representatives "Kentucky House of Representatives") from 2000 to 2012. He unsuccessfully sought the Republican nomination for [governor of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Kentucky "Governor of Kentucky") in the [2015 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Kentucky_gubernatorial_election "2015 Kentucky gubernatorial election"). A year later, he won the Republican nomination for [Kentucky's 1st congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky's_1st_congressional_district "Kentucky's 1st congressional district") to succeed [Ed Whitfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Whitfield "Ed Whitfield"). On November 8, 2016, Comer won both a full term to the seat for the next Congress and a special election that allowed him to serve the remainder of Whitfield's term.

Comer is likely to run for governor in [2027](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2027_Kentucky_gubernatorial_election "2027 Kentucky gubernatorial election").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-:0-5)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Comer is a native of [Carthage, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carthage,_Tennessee "Carthage, Tennessee"). His parents were Dr. James R. Comer Sr. (a dentist) and Sandra Witcher Comer.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-6) He grew up in [Monroe County, Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monroe_County,_Kentucky "Monroe County, Kentucky"), graduating from Monroe County High School, [Tompkinsville, Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tompkinsville,_Kentucky "Tompkinsville, Kentucky"), in 1990.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-7) He received a BS in Agriculture from [Western Kentucky University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Kentucky_University "Western Kentucky University") in 1993.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-8)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-wkyu-9)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-10) In college he served as president of the Kentucky [Future Farmers of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_FFA_Organization "National FFA Organization").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-11) After college, he and his family started James Comer, Jr. Farms,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Mays-12) a 2,300 acres (950 ha) farm,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-13) and he also co-owns Comer Land & Cattle Co.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-14) He served as a director of the South Central Bank for 12 years.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-wkyu-9) Comer served as president of the Monroe County Chamber of Commerce from 1999 to 2000.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-wkyu-9)

## Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early career")]

### Kentucky House of Representatives

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Kentucky House of Representatives")]

In 2000, Comer was elected to the [Kentucky House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_House_of_Representatives "Kentucky House of Representatives") at the age of 27 following the retirement of incumbent [Billy Polston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Polston "Billy Polston"). Comer defeated Donnie Polston, Billy's wife, for the Republican nomination.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-15)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-16)

### Kentucky commissioner of agriculture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Kentucky commissioner of agriculture")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/James_Comer_Kentucky_National_Guard.jpg/250px-James_Comer_Kentucky_National_Guard.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Comer_Kentucky_National_Guard.jpg)

Comer speaking to members of the [Kentucky National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_National_Guard "Kentucky National Guard") in 2013

In 2011, Comer ran for agriculture commissioner. The incumbent, [Richie Farmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richie_Farmer "Richie Farmer"), was [term-limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Term_limits_in_the_United_States "Term limits in the United States").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-17) In the election, Comer was the only Republican to win election to a statewide executive office,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-18) and worked with a team of Democratic officials and under a Democratic governor.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-19) He had the highest percentage of the vote of any candidate on the ballot, and raised $606,766 to his opponent's $204,287.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-20) He took office in January 2012. One of Comer's first actions in office was to work with Democratic auditor [Adam Edelen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Edelen "Adam Edelen") to investigate his Republican predecessor's ethics while in office.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-21)

That year Comer, became chair of the Kentucky Industrial Hemp Commission,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-22) and shortly after taking office, he called the legalization of industrialized hemp his top priority,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-23)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-24) and was "instrumental in getting the hemp industry up and running",[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-WKM-25) including by founding several pilot programs[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-26) in an effort to restart Kentucky's industrial hemp industry. He also filed suit against the DEA, which resulted in the DEA allowing hemp seeds to be delivered to Kentucky farmers for the first new crops.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-27) Between 2014 and 2015, Kentucky's hemp crops grew from 33 to 1,700 acres.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-28) Comer also advocated for national hemp deregulation.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-29)

Comer founded the Kentucky Proud Farm to Campus program,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-30) and created a mobile science centers program for primary and secondary school students to learn about agricultural sciences.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-31)

## Gubernatorial campaigns

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Gubernatorial campaigns")]

### 2015 gubernatorial election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2015 gubernatorial election")]

Main article: [2015 Kentucky gubernatorial election §Republican primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Kentucky_gubernatorial_election#Republican_primary "2015 Kentucky gubernatorial election")

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/James_Comer_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg/250px-James_Comer_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Comer_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg)

Comer in 2014

On August 2, 2014, during the annual [Fancy Farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fancy_Farm,_Kentucky "Fancy Farm, Kentucky") picnic, Comer announced he would seek the Republican nomination for [governor of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Kentucky "Governor of Kentucky") in the [2015 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Kentucky_gubernatorial_election "2015 Kentucky gubernatorial election").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-32) His running mate was state senator [Christian McDaniel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_McDaniel "Christian McDaniel").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-33) At the conclusion of voting in the May 19 election, Comer was 83 votes behind businessman [Matt Bevin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Bevin "Matt Bevin"). The [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press"), calling the race a "virtual tie", did not call it for either candidate. Comer refused to concede and said he would request a recanvass.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-34) The request was filed with the [Kentucky secretary of state's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Secretary_of_State "Kentucky Secretary of State") office on May 20, with Secretary of State [Alison Lundergan Grimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Lundergan_Grimes "Alison Lundergan Grimes") ordering the recanvass to begin at 9:00 a.m. on May 28.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-35)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-36) After the recanvass, Grimes announced that Bevin remained 83 votes ahead of Comer.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Atl-37) She also said that should Comer want a full [recount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Election_recount "Election recount"), it would require a court order from the [Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_County,_Kentucky "Franklin County, Kentucky")[Circuit Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Circuit_Court "Kentucky Circuit Court").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-38) On May 29, Comer announced he would not request a recount and conceded the nomination to Bevin.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-39)

### 2027 gubernatorial election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2027 gubernatorial election")]

Main article: [2027 Kentucky gubernatorial election §Republican primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2027_Kentucky_gubernatorial_election#Republican_primary "2027 Kentucky gubernatorial election")

On May 7, 2026, Comer stated during a visit to [Greenup County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenup_County,_Kentucky "Greenup County, Kentucky") that he intended to run for governor in [2027](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2027_Kentucky_gubernatorial_election "2027 Kentucky gubernatorial election"), and would likely officially announce his run at the end of the year.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-:0-5) Comer has been regularly cited as a potential candidate for the Republican nomination, and has been open about building a state-wide network in anticipation for the election.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-:0-5)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-41)

#### 2016

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2016")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/James_Comer_swearing_in.jpg/250px-James_Comer_swearing_in.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Comer_swearing_in.jpg)

Comer being sworn in by Speaker [Paul Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Ryan "Paul Ryan")

In 2016, Comer entered the Republican primary election for the 1st congressional district of Kentucky against two other competitors. Before the primary, he was endorsed by the [NRA Political Victory Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRA_Political_Victory_Fund "NRA Political Victory Fund")[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-42) and the [US Chamber of Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Chamber_of_Commerce "United States Chamber of Commerce").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-43) He won the primary with 60.6% of the vote; the real contest in this heavily Republican district.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Atl-37) Since Whitfield had resigned in September, Comer ran in two elections on November 8–a special election for the last two months of Whitfield's 11th term, and a regular election for a full two-year term. Comer won both elections over Democratic nominee Samuel L. Gaskins with over 72% of the vote.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-44) Comer was elected to the House with 72.6% of the vote.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-WKM-25) He was sworn in soon after the results were certified, giving him two months' more seniority over the rest of the 2017 freshman class.

### Tenure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Tenure")]

During his first few months in office, Comer held several town hall meetings, where he discussed the Congress's early platform.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-45) He partnered with [Murray State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_State_University "Murray State University") to form the Congressman James Comer Congressional Agriculture Fellowship program,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-46) and advocated for agricultural legislation reform.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-47) He criticized the regulatory policies of [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama"),[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-48) and supported the early domestic policies and actions of [President Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_Donald_Trump "President Donald Trump"). Comer is a social conservative on same-sex marriage and abortion, which means he is in opposition to both.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-49) He believes the trade embargo on Cuba should be lifted.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-50)

Comer voted for the [Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_Cuts_and_Jobs_Act_of_2017 "Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Almukhtar-51) After the bill passed, he said: "I am proud to support this critical part of President Trump's pro-growth agenda that will fulfill this promise to the American people who have struggled under the weight of Washington bureaucrats for far too long."[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-OCM121917-52)

Comer was an original cosponsor of the Hemp Farming Act, which legalized hemp nationwide and removed federal regulations on the crop.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-53) The bill was later included in the [Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_United_States_farm_bill "2018 United States farm bill") and signed into law by President Trump on December 20, 2018.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-54) Comer was a member of the conference committee that negotiated its final version.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-55)

At the outset of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), Comer and Representative [Suzanne Bonamici](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzanne_Bonamici "Suzanne Bonamici") introduced legislation that would protect access to school lunches for school districts throughout the country that had to close because of the pandemic.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-wkms.org-56) The COVID-19 Child Nutrition Response Act allows the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to waive requirements for children to gather at schools for school officials and food service personnel to distribute reimbursable, nutritious meals. It also gives local school officials discretion over substitutions for meal components if supply or procurement is disrupted.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-wtvq.com-57) When introducing the bill, Comer said, "this bill is a critical step toward ensuring that our students maintain access to the school meals they rely on for their health and well-being".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-wkms.org-56) After it cleared the House and Senate, President Trump signed the legislation into law on March 18.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-wtvq.com-57)

After the [2022 United States House of Representatives election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election "2022 United States House of Representatives election") resulted in a House Republican majority, Comer said that the House Oversight Committee's "focus in this next Congress" would be to investigate President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden"), particularly his "relationship with his family's foreign partners and whether he is a president who is compromised or swayed by foreign dollars and influence".[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-58)

After Comer became chair of the Oversight Committee, he responded in January 2023 to the [Joe Biden classified documents incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden_classified_documents_incident "Joe Biden classified documents incident") by calling for visitor logs for Biden's residence, where Biden's lawyers found some classified documents from his vice presidency; the same day, Comer said that he would not call for visitor logs for Trump's residence [Mar-a-Lago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar-a-Lago "Mar-a-Lago"), where [an FBI search found classified documents from Trump's presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FBI_search_of_Mar-a-Lago "FBI search of Mar-a-Lago") despite Trump's lawyers' claim that no such documents were there.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-59) Comer declared he would investigate Biden because Biden "hasn't been investigated", adding: "there have been so many investigations of President Trump. I don't feel like we need to spend a whole lot of time investigating President Trump".[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-60) When Comer told Fox TV's [Sean Hannity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Hannity "Sean Hannity"), "You look at how Donald Trump is treated. He had documents in one location behind a locked door," Florida Democratic congressman [Jared Moskowitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jared_Moskowitz "Jared Moskowitz") aired previously publicly widely distributed footage of large quantities boxes of classified and confidential documents in [Mar-a-Lago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar-a-Lago "Mar-a-Lago") were haphazardly stored in various places including an unlocked bathroom and on a theater stage.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-61) In March 2023, Comer confirmed that he had ended a House investigation into Trump's financial dealings, in which Trump's former accounting company, [Mazars USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazars_USA "Mazars USA"), had been turning over documents as part of a court-supervised settlement; the documents provided information on how foreign governments patronized the Trump International Hotel. Comer said he "didn’t even know who or what Mazars was" and that he was instead investigating "money the Bidens received from China".[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-62)

When CNN asked Comer in April 2023 whether his investigation had found "anything illegal while [Joe Biden] was actually in office", he replied: "we found a lot that's certainly unethical … We found a lot that should be illegal. The line is blurry as to what is legal and not legal with respect to family influence-peddling."[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-63)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-64) On September 12, 2023, Speaker [Kevin McCarthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_McCarthy "Kevin McCarthy") announced an [impeachment inquiry into Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_inquiry_into_Joe_Biden "Impeachment inquiry into Joe Biden"), and announced that he had chosen Comer to head the inquiry.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-65)

Comer discussed the impeachment inquiry into Joe Biden in October 2023, stating that "because we have so many documents, and we can bring these people in for [private] depositions or [public] committee hearings, whichever they choose".[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Emily-66) After Biden's son Hunter was subpoenaed to testify, Hunter preferred to testify publicly instead of privately, to avoid misrepresentations of the proceedings, stated Hunter's lawyer; Comer responded that the subpoenas for a private deposition were "not mere suggestions open to [Hunter] Biden's interpretation or preference".[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Emily-66)

In March 2024, Comer declared: "I am preparing criminal referrals as the culmination of my investigation" for the impeachment inquiry into Joe Biden.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-67) In June 2024, Comer made criminal referrals of Hunter Biden and James Biden to the Justice Department, over alleged refusal to provide information that _[The Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hill\_(newspaper) "The Hill (newspaper)")_ reported had "limited connection" to Joe Biden.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-68) Later that month Comer insisted that "this is an investigation of Joe Biden … This was always about Joe Biden … the next step will be accountability for Joe Biden."[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-69) In August 2024, _The Washington Post_ reported that Comer's "investigation quietly sputtered out after no evidence or testimony obtained by congressional Republicans showed that the president was a direct participant in or beneficiary of his family’s business dealings … Comer himself also promised multiple criminal referrals against [Joe] Biden that never materialized."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Praveena-4)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/37/James_Comer_%2854346937749%29.jpg/250px-James_Comer_%2854346937749%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Comer_(54346937749).jpg)

Comer at 2025 [CPAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Political_Action_Conference "Conservative Political Action Conference")

After Joe Biden ended his 2024 presidential re-election campaign and Vice President [Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris") became the Democratic Party presidential nominee, Comer in August 2024 announced an investigation into Harris' actions in regard to [U.S. Customs and Border Protection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Customs_and_Border_Protection "U.S. Customs and Border Protection") and the [United States-Mexico border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States-Mexico_border "United States-Mexico border"), with Comer declaring that it was "unclear what actions, if any, Vice President Harris has taken to fix the border crisis".[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-70) Later in August 2024, Comer announced another investigation, this time on the Democratic Party's vice-presidential nominee, [Tim Walz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Walz "Tim Walz"), the governor of Minnesota, as Comer asked the [Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") to provide information on Walz in relation to China.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-71)

In July 2026, Comer introduced legislation requiring additional congressional approval for any changes in taxes and fees by the local [Washington, D.C. government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C._government "Washington, D.C. government").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-72)

## Political positions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Political positions")]

### Health care

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Health care")]

Comer supports the repeal of the [Affordable Care Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act "Affordable Care Act") ("Obamacare").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-VS2016-79)

### Economic issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Economic issues")]

In 2016 Comer called the Obama administration's final budget a "disaster in the making".[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In 2017, he voted for the [Tax Cuts and Jobs Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_Cuts_and_Jobs_Act_of_2017 "Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017"), also denoted as the "Trump tax cuts", which was estimated to add $1.49 trillion to the national debt.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Bryan111017-80)

Comer opposes paid [parental leave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parental_leave "Parental leave") for federal workers.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-81)

### Immigration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Immigration")]

Comer opposes [amnesty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty "Amnesty") and [sanctuary cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanctuary_cities "Sanctuary cities"). He supports [Executive Order 13767](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_Order_13767 "Executive Order 13767"), the building of a wall along the [Mexico–U.S. border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico%E2%80%93United_States_border "Mexico–United States border").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-VS2016-79)

### Abortion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Abortion")]

Comer is anti-abortion.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-VS2016-79)

### Marijuana

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Marijuana")]

Comer supports declassifying [marijuana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marijuana "Marijuana") as a Schedule 1 narcotic and growing [hemp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemp "Hemp"). In December 2017, he said there is "simply not enough support for medical marijuana legalization across the board".[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Harvey122317-82)

### LGBT rights

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: LGBT rights")]

Comer opposes [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage "Same-sex marriage").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-VS2016-79) He also opposes banning [discrimination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrimination "Discrimination") based on [sexual orientation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_orientation "Sexual orientation") and [gender identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender_identity "Gender identity"), and voted against the [Equality Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equality_Act_(United_States) "Equality Act (United States)") in 2019.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-83)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-84) Comer voted against the [Respect for Marriage Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respect_for_Marriage_Act "Respect for Marriage Act") in 2022.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-85)

### Environment

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Environment")]

In 2015, Comer said he did not [believe in climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change_denial "Climate change denial"). Comer said “We've had a very severe winter this year with 12-inch snows, so there is no global warming.”[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-86) .

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Comer is married to Tamara Jo "TJ" Comer and has three children. He was baptized at First Baptist Church of Tompkinsville and is a member of Elkhorn Baptist Church in Midway, Kentucky.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-VoteSmart-3)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-104)

### Personal finances

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Personal finances")]

In 2015, just before Comer started publicly running for Congress, he bought a 50% stake in six acres of Kentucky land for $128,000 from landowner Darren Cleary, a major donor to Comer's political campaigns.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Slodysko-105) In 2017, Comer transferred this stake to a [shell company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shell_company "Shell company"), Farm Team Properties, that Comer owns with his wife.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Slodysko-105)

Comer reported that Farm Team Companies was worth at least $500,000 in 2022, but it was "not clear" if the shell company owned any other assets, reported the Associated Press in 2023.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Slodysko-105) In 2020, Comer was criticized for stock trading ahead of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic")-related [2020 stock market crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_stock_market_crash "2020 stock market crash"): Comer reportedly dumped shares in [Bank of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_America "Bank of America") and purchased shares of online workplace messaging company [Slack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slack_(software) "Slack (software)").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-106)

By 2023, Comer has reported owning around 1,600 acres of land.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Slodysko-105)

### Abuse allegations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Abuse allegations")]

On May 5, 2015, Comer was accused of physical and mental abuse by Marilyn Thomas, a woman he dated while attending Western Kentucky University in 1993.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-107) He has said he believes the accusation was a political stunt to hinder his gubernatorial campaign.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Atl-37)

**James Richardson Comer Jr.**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-VoteSmart-3) ([/ˈ k oʊ m ər/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_KOH-mər_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born August 19, 1972) is an American politician serving as the [U.S. Representative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Representative "U.S. Representative") for [Kentucky's 1st congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky's_1st_congressional_district "Kentucky's 1st congressional district"). A member of the [Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"), he has served in Congress since 2016, during the [114th United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/114th_United_States_Congress "114th United States Congress"). He previously served in the [Kentucky House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_House_of_Representatives "Kentucky House of Representatives") and also served as the [agriculture commissioner of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture_Commissioner_of_Kentucky "Agriculture Commissioner of Kentucky").

As the chair of the [Oversight Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_Oversight_and_Government_Reform "United States House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform") from 2023, Comer has declined or stopped investigations into former president [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump"), while starting an investigation on President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") and his family. As of August 2024, Comer's investigation has yet to unearth evidence that Biden was directly involved in or profited from his family's business activities.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Praveena-4) After Biden ended his 2024 presidential re-election campaign, Comer began an investigation into the new Democratic presidential nominee, Vice President [Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris"), and also began an investigation into the new Democratic vice-presidential nominee, Governor [Tim Walz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Walz "Tim Walz").

Comer served as Kentucky's agriculture commissioner from 2012 to 2016 and in the [Kentucky House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_House_of_Representatives "Kentucky House of Representatives") from 2000 to 2012. He unsuccessfully sought the Republican nomination for [governor of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Kentucky "Governor of Kentucky") in the [2015 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Kentucky_gubernatorial_election "2015 Kentucky gubernatorial election"). A year later, he won the Republican nomination for [Kentucky's 1st congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky's_1st_congressional_district "Kentucky's 1st congressional district") to succeed [Ed Whitfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Whitfield "Ed Whitfield"). On November 8, 2016, Comer won both a full term to the seat for the next Congress and a special election that allowed him to serve the remainder of Whitfield's term.

Comer is likely to run for governor in [2027](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2027_Kentucky_gubernatorial_election "2027 Kentucky gubernatorial election").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-:0-5)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Comer is a native of [Carthage, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carthage,_Tennessee "Carthage, Tennessee"). His parents were Dr. James R. Comer Sr. (a dentist) and Sandra Witcher Comer.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-6) He grew up in [Monroe County, Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monroe_County,_Kentucky "Monroe County, Kentucky"), graduating from Monroe County High School, [Tompkinsville, Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tompkinsville,_Kentucky "Tompkinsville, Kentucky"), in 1990.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-7) He received a BS in Agriculture from [Western Kentucky University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Kentucky_University "Western Kentucky University") in 1993.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-8)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-wkyu-9)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-10) In college he served as president of the Kentucky [Future Farmers of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_FFA_Organization "National FFA Organization").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-11) After college, he and his family started James Comer, Jr. Farms,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Mays-12) a 2,300 acres (950 ha) farm,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-13) and he also co-owns Comer Land & Cattle Co.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-14) He served as a director of the South Central Bank for 12 years.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-wkyu-9) Comer served as president of the Monroe County Chamber of Commerce from 1999 to 2000.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-wkyu-9)

## Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early career")]

### Kentucky House of Representatives

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Kentucky House of Representatives")]

In 2000, Comer was elected to the [Kentucky House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_House_of_Representatives "Kentucky House of Representatives") at the age of 27 following the retirement of incumbent [Billy Polston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Polston "Billy Polston"). Comer defeated Donnie Polston, Billy's wife, for the Republican nomination.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-15)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-16)

### Kentucky commissioner of agriculture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Kentucky commissioner of agriculture")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/James_Comer_Kentucky_National_Guard.jpg/250px-James_Comer_Kentucky_National_Guard.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Comer_Kentucky_National_Guard.jpg)

Comer speaking to members of the [Kentucky National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_National_Guard "Kentucky National Guard") in 2013

In 2011, Comer ran for agriculture commissioner. The incumbent, [Richie Farmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richie_Farmer "Richie Farmer"), was [term-limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Term_limits_in_the_United_States "Term limits in the United States").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-17) In the election, Comer was the only Republican to win election to a statewide executive office,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-18) and worked with a team of Democratic officials and under a Democratic governor.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-19) He had the highest percentage of the vote of any candidate on the ballot, and raised $606,766 to his opponent's $204,287.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-20) He took office in January 2012. One of Comer's first actions in office was to work with Democratic auditor [Adam Edelen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Edelen "Adam Edelen") to investigate his Republican predecessor's ethics while in office.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-21)

That year Comer, became chair of the Kentucky Industrial Hemp Commission,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-22) and shortly after taking office, he called the legalization of industrialized hemp his top priority,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-23)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-24) and was "instrumental in getting the hemp industry up and running",[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-WKM-25) including by founding several pilot programs[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-26) in an effort to restart Kentucky's industrial hemp industry. He also filed suit against the DEA, which resulted in the DEA allowing hemp seeds to be delivered to Kentucky farmers for the first new crops.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-27) Between 2014 and 2015, Kentucky's hemp crops grew from 33 to 1,700 acres.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-28) Comer also advocated for national hemp deregulation.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-29)

Comer founded the Kentucky Proud Farm to Campus program,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-30) and created a mobile science centers program for primary and secondary school students to learn about agricultural sciences.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-31)

## Gubernatorial campaigns

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Gubernatorial campaigns")]

### 2015 gubernatorial election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2015 gubernatorial election")]

Main article: [2015 Kentucky gubernatorial election §Republican primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Kentucky_gubernatorial_election#Republican_primary "2015 Kentucky gubernatorial election")

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/James_Comer_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg/250px-James_Comer_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Comer_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg)

Comer in 2014

On August 2, 2014, during the annual [Fancy Farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fancy_Farm,_Kentucky "Fancy Farm, Kentucky") picnic, Comer announced he would seek the Republican nomination for [governor of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Kentucky "Governor of Kentucky") in the [2015 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Kentucky_gubernatorial_election "2015 Kentucky gubernatorial election").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-32) His running mate was state senator [Christian McDaniel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_McDaniel "Christian McDaniel").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-33) At the conclusion of voting in the May 19 election, Comer was 83 votes behind businessman [Matt Bevin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Bevin "Matt Bevin"). The [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press"), calling the race a "virtual tie", did not call it for either candidate. Comer refused to concede and said he would request a recanvass.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-34) The request was filed with the [Kentucky secretary of state's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Secretary_of_State "Kentucky Secretary of State") office on May 20, with Secretary of State [Alison Lundergan Grimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Lundergan_Grimes "Alison Lundergan Grimes") ordering the recanvass to begin at 9:00 a.m. on May 28.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-35)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-36) After the recanvass, Grimes announced that Bevin remained 83 votes ahead of Comer.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Atl-37) She also said that should Comer want a full [recount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Election_recount "Election recount"), it would require a court order from the [Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_County,_Kentucky "Franklin County, Kentucky")[Circuit Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Circuit_Court "Kentucky Circuit Court").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-38) On May 29, Comer announced he would not request a recount and conceded the nomination to Bevin.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-39)

### 2027 gubernatorial election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2027 gubernatorial election")]

Main article: [2027 Kentucky gubernatorial election §Republican primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2027_Kentucky_gubernatorial_election#Republican_primary "2027 Kentucky gubernatorial election")

On May 7, 2026, Comer stated during a visit to [Greenup County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenup_County,_Kentucky "Greenup County, Kentucky") that he intended to run for governor in [2027](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2027_Kentucky_gubernatorial_election "2027 Kentucky gubernatorial election"), and would likely officially announce his run at the end of the year.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-:0-5) Comer has been regularly cited as a potential candidate for the Republican nomination, and has been open about building a state-wide network in anticipation for the election.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-:0-5)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-41)

#### 2016

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2016")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/James_Comer_swearing_in.jpg/250px-James_Comer_swearing_in.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Comer_swearing_in.jpg)

Comer being sworn in by Speaker [Paul Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Ryan "Paul Ryan")

In 2016, Comer entered the Republican primary election for the 1st congressional district of Kentucky against two other competitors. Before the primary, he was endorsed by the [NRA Political Victory Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRA_Political_Victory_Fund "NRA Political Victory Fund")[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-42) and the [US Chamber of Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Chamber_of_Commerce "United States Chamber of Commerce").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-43) He won the primary with 60.6% of the vote; the real contest in this heavily Republican district.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Atl-37) Since Whitfield had resigned in September, Comer ran in two elections on November 8–a special election for the last two months of Whitfield's 11th term, and a regular election for a full two-year term. Comer won both elections over Democratic nominee Samuel L. Gaskins with over 72% of the vote.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-44) Comer was elected to the House with 72.6% of the vote.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-WKM-25) He was sworn in soon after the results were certified, giving him two months' more seniority over the rest of the 2017 freshman class.

### Tenure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Tenure")]

During his first few months in office, Comer held several town hall meetings, where he discussed the Congress's early platform.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-45) He partnered with [Murray State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_State_University "Murray State University") to form the Congressman James Comer Congressional Agriculture Fellowship program,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-46) and advocated for agricultural legislation reform.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-47) He criticized the regulatory policies of [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama"),[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-48) and supported the early domestic policies and actions of [President Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_Donald_Trump "President Donald Trump"). Comer is a social conservative on same-sex marriage and abortion, which means he is in opposition to both.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-49) He believes the trade embargo on Cuba should be lifted.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-50)

Comer voted for the [Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_Cuts_and_Jobs_Act_of_2017 "Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Almukhtar-51) After the bill passed, he said: "I am proud to support this critical part of President Trump's pro-growth agenda that will fulfill this promise to the American people who have struggled under the weight of Washington bureaucrats for far too long."[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-OCM121917-52)

Comer was an original cosponsor of the Hemp Farming Act, which legalized hemp nationwide and removed federal regulations on the crop.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-53) The bill was later included in the [Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_United_States_farm_bill "2018 United States farm bill") and signed into law by President Trump on December 20, 2018.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-54) Comer was a member of the conference committee that negotiated its final version.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-55)

At the outset of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), Comer and Representative [Suzanne Bonamici](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzanne_Bonamici "Suzanne Bonamici") introduced legislation that would protect access to school lunches for school districts throughout the country that had to close because of the pandemic.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-wkms.org-56) The COVID-19 Child Nutrition Response Act allows the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to waive requirements for children to gather at schools for school officials and food service personnel to distribute reimbursable, nutritious meals. It also gives local school officials discretion over substitutions for meal components if supply or procurement is disrupted.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-wtvq.com-57) When introducing the bill, Comer said, "this bill is a critical step toward ensuring that our students maintain access to the school meals they rely on for their health and well-being".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-wkms.org-56) After it cleared the House and Senate, President Trump signed the legislation into law on March 18.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-wtvq.com-57)

After the [2022 United States House of Representatives election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election "2022 United States House of Representatives election") resulted in a House Republican majority, Comer said that the House Oversight Committee's "focus in this next Congress" would be to investigate President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden"), particularly his "relationship with his family's foreign partners and whether he is a president who is compromised or swayed by foreign dollars and influence".[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-58)

After Comer became chair of the Oversight Committee, he responded in January 2023 to the [Joe Biden classified documents incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden_classified_documents_incident "Joe Biden classified documents incident") by calling for visitor logs for Biden's residence, where Biden's lawyers found some classified documents from his vice presidency; the same day, Comer said that he would not call for visitor logs for Trump's residence [Mar-a-Lago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar-a-Lago "Mar-a-Lago"), where [an FBI search found classified documents from Trump's presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FBI_search_of_Mar-a-Lago "FBI search of Mar-a-Lago") despite Trump's lawyers' claim that no such documents were there.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-59) Comer declared he would investigate Biden because Biden "hasn't been investigated", adding: "there have been so many investigations of President Trump. I don't feel like we need to spend a whole lot of time investigating President Trump".[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-60) When Comer told Fox TV's [Sean Hannity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Hannity "Sean Hannity"), "You look at how Donald Trump is treated. He had documents in one location behind a locked door," Florida Democratic congressman [Jared Moskowitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jared_Moskowitz "Jared Moskowitz") aired previously publicly widely distributed footage of large quantities boxes of classified and confidential documents in [Mar-a-Lago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar-a-Lago "Mar-a-Lago") were haphazardly stored in various places including an unlocked bathroom and on a theater stage.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-61) In March 2023, Comer confirmed that he had ended a House investigation into Trump's financial dealings, in which Trump's former accounting company, [Mazars USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazars_USA "Mazars USA"), had been turning over documents as part of a court-supervised settlement; the documents provided information on how foreign governments patronized the Trump International Hotel. Comer said he "didn’t even know who or what Mazars was" and that he was instead investigating "money the Bidens received from China".[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-62)

When CNN asked Comer in April 2023 whether his investigation had found "anything illegal while [Joe Biden] was actually in office", he replied: "we found a lot that's certainly unethical … We found a lot that should be illegal. The line is blurry as to what is legal and not legal with respect to family influence-peddling."[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-63)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-64) On September 12, 2023, Speaker [Kevin McCarthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_McCarthy "Kevin McCarthy") announced an [impeachment inquiry into Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_inquiry_into_Joe_Biden "Impeachment inquiry into Joe Biden"), and announced that he had chosen Comer to head the inquiry.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-65)

Comer discussed the impeachment inquiry into Joe Biden in October 2023, stating that "because we have so many documents, and we can bring these people in for [private] depositions or [public] committee hearings, whichever they choose".[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Emily-66) After Biden's son Hunter was subpoenaed to testify, Hunter preferred to testify publicly instead of privately, to avoid misrepresentations of the proceedings, stated Hunter's lawyer; Comer responded that the subpoenas for a private deposition were "not mere suggestions open to [Hunter] Biden's interpretation or preference".[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Emily-66)

In March 2024, Comer declared: "I am preparing criminal referrals as the culmination of my investigation" for the impeachment inquiry into Joe Biden.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-67) In June 2024, Comer made criminal referrals of Hunter Biden and James Biden to the Justice Department, over alleged refusal to provide information that _[The Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hill\_(newspaper) "The Hill (newspaper)")_ reported had "limited connection" to Joe Biden.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-68) Later that month Comer insisted that "this is an investigation of Joe Biden … This was always about Joe Biden … the next step will be accountability for Joe Biden."[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-69) In August 2024, _The Washington Post_ reported that Comer's "investigation quietly sputtered out after no evidence or testimony obtained by congressional Republicans showed that the president was a direct participant in or beneficiary of his family’s business dealings … Comer himself also promised multiple criminal referrals against [Joe] Biden that never materialized."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Praveena-4)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/37/James_Comer_%2854346937749%29.jpg/250px-James_Comer_%2854346937749%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Comer_(54346937749).jpg)

Comer at 2025 [CPAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Political_Action_Conference "Conservative Political Action Conference")

After Joe Biden ended his 2024 presidential re-election campaign and Vice President [Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris") became the Democratic Party presidential nominee, Comer in August 2024 announced an investigation into Harris' actions in regard to [U.S. Customs and Border Protection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Customs_and_Border_Protection "U.S. Customs and Border Protection") and the [United States-Mexico border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States-Mexico_border "United States-Mexico border"), with Comer declaring that it was "unclear what actions, if any, Vice President Harris has taken to fix the border crisis".[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-70) Later in August 2024, Comer announced another investigation, this time on the Democratic Party's vice-presidential nominee, [Tim Walz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Walz "Tim Walz"), the governor of Minnesota, as Comer asked the [Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") to provide information on Walz in relation to China.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-71)

In July 2026, Comer introduced legislation requiring additional congressional approval for any changes in taxes and fees by the local [Washington, D.C. government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C._government "Washington, D.C. government").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-72)

## Political positions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Political positions")]

### Health care

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Health care")]

Comer supports the repeal of the [Affordable Care Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act "Affordable Care Act") ("Obamacare").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-VS2016-79)

### Economic issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Economic issues")]

In 2016 Comer called the Obama administration's final budget a "disaster in the making".[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In 2017, he voted for the [Tax Cuts and Jobs Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_Cuts_and_Jobs_Act_of_2017 "Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017"), also denoted as the "Trump tax cuts", which was estimated to add $1.49 trillion to the national debt.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Bryan111017-80)

Comer opposes paid [parental leave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parental_leave "Parental leave") for federal workers.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-81)

### Immigration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Immigration")]

Comer opposes [amnesty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty "Amnesty") and [sanctuary cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanctuary_cities "Sanctuary cities"). He supports [Executive Order 13767](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_Order_13767 "Executive Order 13767"), the building of a wall along the [Mexico–U.S. border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico%E2%80%93United_States_border "Mexico–United States border").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-VS2016-79)

### Abortion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Abortion")]

Comer is anti-abortion.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-VS2016-79)

### Marijuana

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Marijuana")]

Comer supports declassifying [marijuana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marijuana "Marijuana") as a Schedule 1 narcotic and growing [hemp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemp "Hemp"). In December 2017, he said there is "simply not enough support for medical marijuana legalization across the board".[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Harvey122317-82)

### LGBT rights

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: LGBT rights")]

Comer opposes [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage "Same-sex marriage").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-VS2016-79) He also opposes banning [discrimination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrimination "Discrimination") based on [sexual orientation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_orientation "Sexual orientation") and [gender identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender_identity "Gender identity"), and voted against the [Equality Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equality_Act_(United_States) "Equality Act (United States)") in 2019.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-83)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-84) Comer voted against the [Respect for Marriage Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respect_for_Marriage_Act "Respect for Marriage Act") in 2022.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-85)

### Environment

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Environment")]

In 2015, Comer said he did not [believe in climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change_denial "Climate change denial"). Comer said “We've had a very severe winter this year with 12-inch snows, so there is no global warming.”[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-86) .

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Comer is married to Tamara Jo "TJ" Comer and has three children. He was baptized at First Baptist Church of Tompkinsville and is a member of Elkhorn Baptist Church in Midway, Kentucky.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-VoteSmart-3)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-104)

### Personal finances

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Personal finances")]

In 2015, just before Comer started publicly running for Congress, he bought a 50% stake in six acres of Kentucky land for $128,000 from landowner Darren Cleary, a major donor to Comer's political campaigns.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Slodysko-105) In 2017, Comer transferred this stake to a [shell company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shell_company "Shell company"), Farm Team Properties, that Comer owns with his wife.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Slodysko-105)

Comer reported that Farm Team Companies was worth at least $500,000 in 2022, but it was "not clear" if the shell company owned any other assets, reported the Associated Press in 2023.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Slodysko-105) In 2020, Comer was criticized for stock trading ahead of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic")-related [2020 stock market crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_stock_market_crash "2020 stock market crash"): Comer reportedly dumped shares in [Bank of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_America "Bank of America") and purchased shares of online workplace messaging company [Slack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slack_(software) "Slack (software)").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-106)

By 2023, Comer has reported owning around 1,600 acres of land.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Slodysko-105)

### Abuse allegations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Comer&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Abuse allegations")]

On May 5, 2015, Comer was accused of physical and mental abuse by Marilyn Thomas, a woman he dated while attending Western Kentucky University in 1993.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-107) He has said he believes the accusation was a political stunt to hinder his gubernatorial campaign.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Comer#cite_note-Atl-37)
